questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The metal hydroxide which is soluble in excess of ammonium hydroxide is
questions.solution: Copper (II) hydroxide $\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}\right]$ is amphoteric in nature and is soluble in excess of ammonium hydroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the detection of III group basic radicals $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OH}$ is added after $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}$ to
options: increase in the ionisation of salt solution
decrease in the jonisation of salt solution
questions.solution: In the detection of III group, basic radicals $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OH}$ is added after $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}$ to decrease the ionisation of $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OII}$ due to common ion effect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The brown ring test for nitrates depends on
options: the reduction of nitrate to nitric oxide
oxidation of nitric oxide to nitrogen dioxide
reduction of ferrous sulphate to iron
questions.solution:
The brown ring is appeared due to formation of a brown complex between nitric oxide and $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ion.
This nitric oxide is formed as a result of reduction of nitrate. Brown ring test for nitrates depends on reduction of nitrate to nitric oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In qualitative analysis, in order to detect second group basic radical, $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{ S}$ gas is passed in the presence of dilute HCl to
options: increase the dissociation of salt solution
decrease the dissociation of salt solution
questions.solution: On passing $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{ S}$ gas in presence of dil. $\mathrm{HCl}$ for qualitative analysis of second group due to common ion effect, lower concentration of sulphide ions is obtained. It is sufficient for the precipitation of second group cations in forms of their sulphides and hence their dissociation decreases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound which produces a bluish green flame when heated on a copper wire is
questions.solution:
An organic compound containing halogen produces a bluish green flame when heated on a copper wire. This test is called Beilstein's test.
$\therefore$ Chlorobenzene will produce bluish green flame when heated on copper wire.
